rulers.note: Named as Mahmud's successor; his end is bridged by Nasir-ud-Din's accession on 22 October 1510.

ledger.note: 1401: Dilawar Khan makes Malwa an independent realm at Dhar. 'following Timur's invasion and the disintegration of the Delhi Sultanate, in 1401, made Malwa an independent realm'; Dilawar Khan 'had ceased to pay tribute to Delhi after 1392'; infobox 'Established: 1401'. The page gives no boundary.

region.text: Malwa around Dhar, held by a Gujarat governor

ledger.note: 1407: Gujarat takes Dhar. 'In 1407, he reached the capital Dhar, where Sultan Hoshang Shah confronted him'; Hoshang was arrested, 'Malwa was annexed by Gujarat Sultanate' and Nusrat Khan was set over it; the page gives no year for the governor.

1409: Hoshang Shah is back in Malwa. The page gives no year for his release ('Hushang Shah was released as situation went out of hands'; the Malwa nobles 'elected Musa Khan, Hoshang's cousin, as their leader by December 1408'); the infobox reign runs from 1409.

1410: the capital moves from Dhar to Mandu. 'Hoshang then transferred the capital to Mandu'; the page gives no year, so the move is placed after his restoration; the Malwa page says Mandu was renamed Shadiabad.
1420: Hoshang's war on Kherla begins. Infobox 'Conquest of Kherla (1420-1433)'.
1433: the conquest of Kherla ends. Infobox 'Conquest of Kherla (1420-1433)'.
1433: Kherla is Malwa's. The infobox dates the conquest to 1420-1433 and the page does not say how Kherla was held after; the end year of the span is used.

1436: the Khalji dynasty replaces the Ghurids. 'The Ghurid dynasty... was replaced by Mahmud Shah I, who proclaimed himself king' (Malwa page: 16 May 1436); Mahmud's page has 'ascending the throne on 14 May 1436'. Same state, same colour.

1444: Gagron falls to Mahmud. 'In February 1444, Sultan Mahmud Khalji besieged the fort of Gagron'; the defender Palhan Singh was killed 'while trying to flee'. (Hoshang's infobox has a 1423 siege of Gagron.)

1457 (bridging): Mahmud takes Ajmer. 'Sultan Mahmud Khalji invaded and captured the fort of Ajmer' (Mahmud Khalji page; no year, listed after the capture of Mandalgarh in October 1457, inside his wars with Rana Kumbha of 1442-1457); the Rana Kumbha page: 'Sultan of Malwa took Mewar territories up to Ajmer'. Mirrors the loss in kingdom-of-mewar. [Repair 2026-10-20: new event.]

1457: Mahmud takes Mandalgarh. 'he successfully captured the fort in October 1457' after an earlier attack failed; the page places it in his wars with Rana Kumbha of Mewar (1442-1446 and later), so the loser is read as Mewar.

region.text: much of the Sultanate, ruled by Medini Rai under the lordship of the Rana

ledger.note: 1519: Rana Sanga overruns Malwa. After the Battle of Gagron 'much of the Sultanate came under the brief control of Maharana of Mewar Rana Sanga', who 'appointed one of his vassals, Medini Rai, to rule over the Sultanate'; Medini Rai had been wazir since 1511 and held Chanderi.

1528: Medini Rai falls at Chanderi. The infobox gives his service as 1511-1528 and says he 'was later killed in the Battle of Chanderi against the Mughal emperor Babur'; the Malwa page does not date the end of the Mewar hold, so 1528 is a bridging year.

ledger.counterpart: Gujarat Sultanate (Ajmer), then Biram Dev of Merta
ledger.note: 1531 (bridging): Ajmer leaves the Malwa shape. The Maldeo Rathore page has 'Biram Dev of Merta had recently won Ajmer from the Gujarat Sultanate' before 1534, so Ajmer was Gujarat's by then; when and how it passed from Malwa is not on any page opened, and 1531, the year Gujarat annexed Malwa, is a bridging year. The counterpart is a description, not gujarat-sultanate, whose ledger has no Ajmer gain. [Repair 2026-10-20: new event.]

region.text: Malwa, annexed to Bahadur Shah's kingdom

ledger.note: 1531: Mandu falls and Gujarat annexes Malwa. 'The fortress at Mandu fell and Sultan Mahmud and his seven sons were captured without any resistance on 28 March 1531' (Bahadur Shah page); the Malwa page gives 25 May 1531. Mahmud Shah II had been Gujarat's vassal since 1518.

region.text: a part of the old kingdom

ledger.note: 1537: Qadir Shah regains part of the kingdom. 'Qadir Shah, an ex-officer of the previous Khalji dynasty rulers, regained control over a part of the erstwhile kingdom'; the page names no towns.
1542: Sher Shah Suri conquers Malwa. 'in 1542, Sher Shah Suri conquered the kingdom, defeating him and appointed Shuja'at Khan as the governor.'
1555: Baz Bahadur declares himself independent. 'His son, Baz Bahadur, declared himself independent in 1555'; his reign runs 1555-1562 (infobox of his page).

region.text: Malwa, fought over by Baz Bahadur and the Mughals

ledger.note: 1561: the Mughals invade Malwa. Baz Bahadur was 'defeated... in the battle of Sarangpur on 29 March 1561' by Akbar's forces under Adham Khan and Pir Muhammad Khan; after Pir Muhammad's defeat by a coalition of Khandesh, Berar and Baz Bahadur he 'regained his kingdom for a brief period' (undated).
1562: the Mughals win Malwa. 'Akbar sent another army, led by Abdullah Khan, an Uzbeg, which finally defeated Baz Bahadur', who 'fled to Chittor'.
1562: the Malwa Sultanate becomes the Mughal Malwa Subah. The territory 'became the Malwa Subah (top-level province) of the Mughal empire, with seat at Ujjain'; infobox 'Disestablished: 1562'.

wars.name: Gujarat-Malwa wars
wars.outcome: Gujarat held Dhar in 1407-1409, raided Malwa in 1419, 1420, 1422 and 1438 and annexed it in 1531; Malwa and Khandesh's attack on Gujarat in 1417 failed.
wars.note: Mahmud Khalji also invaded Gujarat and took Champaner before Ahmad Shah II beat him at Kapadvanj (year not given, Mahmud Khalji page).

wars.name: Conquest of Kherla
wars.outcome: Kherla was conquered and became part of Malwa.

wars.name: Malwa invasion of Orissa
wars.outcome: A raid; the Hoshang Shah page gives only 'Invasion of Orissa (1422)' and no land changed hands.

wars.name: Siege of Gagron (1423)
wars.outcome: The infobox lists the siege; the fort is taken by Mahmud Khalji in 1444.

wars.name: Kalpi War
wars.outcome: The infobox lists the war; the page says Kalpi's suzerainty came through a marriage alliance and gives no territory or year for it.

wars.name: Malwa-Mewar wars
wars.outcome: Rana Kumbha defeated and captured Mahmud Khalji at Mandavgad in 1437; battles followed in 1442-1446; Mahmud took Mandalgarh in October 1457.
wars.note: 'Rana Kumbha of Mewar defeated and captured Mahmud Khalji of Malwa for a short period.'

wars.name: Battle of Gagron (1519)
wars.outcome: Rana Sanga defeated Mahmud Shah II of Malwa (and the Gujarat contingent) and put Medini Rai over much of Malwa.

wars.name: Gujarat's conquest of Malwa
wars.outcome: Mandu fell to Bahadur Shah on 28 March 1531; Malwa was annexed to Gujarat.

wars.name: Sur conquest of Malwa
wars.outcome: Sher Shah Suri defeated Qadir Shah in 1542 and appointed Shuja'at Khan governor.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Malwa
wars.outcome: Baz Bahadur lost at Sarangpur on 29 March 1561, regained Malwa with a Khandesh-Berar coalition, and was finally defeated by Abdullah Khan in 1562.

certainty.note: No treaty line is given on any page opened; the Rajasthan frontier with Mewar (Gagron, Mandalgarh) and the Gondwana frontier at Kherla are approximate.

notes:
No Cliopatria row (Cliopatria lacks the Malwa Sultanate; the polities.csv 'malwa-culture' is an unrelated archaeological culture). Five pages plus the Gujarat Sultanate and Bahadur Shah pages for the Gujarat side. None of them gives an area or a boundary, so every keyframe is a reading from the places the pages name; the Malwa region of the gazetteer is the base.
The state is modelled alive to 1562 with two empty keyframes, 1531-1536 (annexed by Gujarat) and 1542-1554 (the Sur Empire's), because the Malwa page gives one infobox span (1401-1562) and Qadir Shah (1537) and Baz Bahadur (1555) are its rulers; the gap-filler may split them. Gujarat's dossier holds Malwa 1531-1537 (and carries Malwa's vassalage to Gujarat from 1518).
Disagreements: Mandu fell 28 March 1531 (Bahadur Shah page) or 25 May 1531 (Malwa page); Mahmud Shah I's accession 14 or 16 May 1436 (and 1435 in the lead of his page); Hoshang's death 5 or 6 July 1435; the infobox gives Hoshang '1409-6 July 1435' and also '1406-1407'.
Not settled: the year of the move to Mandu; Ghazni Khan and the 1435-1436 succession; Ghiyath Shah and Nasir Shah (no events on the pages); Mahmud Khalji's Ajmer and Champaner (undated); Kalpi's suzerainty (no year); Chanderi, Bhilsa and Raisen in the 1510s-1520s (Medini Rai's domain: only Chanderi is named); Qadir Shah's land; the Sur governorship 1542-1555; the year of Baz Bahadur's brief recovery in 1561-1562; the 1561 coalition (Khandesh, Berar).
Counterparts needing a dossier: kingdom-of-mewar (sa-03 successor of guhilas-of-mewar), khandesh-sultanate, sur-empire (sa-05-b), mughal-empire (sa-05-a), Kherla and Gagron (local rulers).
Gazetteer names needed: Kherla, Gagron, Mandalgarh, Dhar.

[Repair 2026-10-20, sa-04-x-fix] Ajmer: the kingdom-of-mewar review found Mewar and Marwar both drawing Ajmer after Mahmud Khalji's capture of it. Mewar now loses it to Malwa in 1457 (this dossier's mirror gain, confidence 1, undated on the Mahmud Khalji page) and Malwa's shape holds it to 1530; the Maldeo Rathore page has Gujarat holding it before Biram Dev of Merta and Maldeo (1534), so a confidence-1 loss in 1531 closes it. Gujarat's ledger carries no Ajmer gain (not changed). Eastern Malwa 1519-1528 stays a contest with kingdom-of-mewar, which dropped its competing gain.
